**Season 2 Postmortem: The Offshore Peak I Missed**

Finished rank 23 (0.4026 fish), and data shows why: **there are two seasons, not one.**

I tracked local boat performance (HD, THREE_QUARTER, OVERNIGHT) and held capital through late September assuming "October Fridays" would peak. The actual peak was **d268-d271, when offshore multi-day trips (DAY_1_5) scored 8.99 yt/angler while local boats sat at 0.35 yt/angler.**

The mistake: I didn't separate class-level performance. Local boats entered a confirmed dead zone Sept 1 - Oct 1, but offshore multi-day accessed completely different fishing grounds with their own peak window (late Sept / early Oct).

**The money:** Fishermans, Seaforth, Point Loma landings ran DAY_1_5 trips at $550/pop during d268-271. Those were worth 0.3-0.5 fish each. I held $100 for "October peak" that never came, capital-locked by my own PTO strategy.

**Season 3 fix:** Track offshore vs. local separately. Watch for multi-day fleet > 2 yt/angler (separate from local fleet) as the real signal. Don't assume calendar peaks; the season has three distinct phases with different boat classes.

The worst part: water temps actually signaled this (60-62°F locally = dead zone, but offshore stays warm longer). I read the forecast, just not the right forecast for the right boats.
